edits.text:
Papilledema on a medication: drug-induced intracranial hypertension Drug causes — retinoids and vitamin A (oral isotretinoin for acne), tetracyclines (minocycline, doxycycline), and growth hormone; the other risk factors are obesity or recent weight gain and being a woman of childbearing age, so a normal-weight adolescent boy still qualifies when the drug is present · The tell — morning headache with nausea and vomiting, transient visual blurring, bilateral papilledema, yet full visual fields (at most an enlarged blind spot) and an otherwise normal neurologic examination; horizontal diplopia from a CN VI palsy, pulsatile tinnitus, and headache worse lying flat may join · Workup order — MRI of the brain (mass, hydrocephalus) → MR venography (venous sinus thrombosis) → LP with opening pressure over 250 mm H2O and normal CSF · Treatment — stop the drug, which usually resolves it; acetazolamide or topiramate to lower CSF pressure, especially with visual loss; weight loss when obesity drives it
Papilledema with full fields: the distractor map Optic chiasm glioma — compresses the chiasm, so expect a bitemporal hemianopsia; full fields argue against it · Optic neuritis — acute vision loss with eye pain, disc swelling usually unilateral, and no morning headache or vomiting · Cluster headache — brief unilateral periorbital or temporal attacks, typically in men aged 20 to 50, with no papilledema · Viral encephalitis — fever and altered mental status, absent in an afebrile, alert teen

items.stem: 16 yo M taking oral isotretinoin for severe acne; 1 month of daily throbbing frontal headache, worse in the morning, with nausea and occasional vomiting; one brief episode of blurred vision in the left eye; BP 130/80; bilateral optic disc edema with decreased visual acuity, full visual fields, equal reactive pupils, no meningismus, normal motor, reflex, and sensory examination
items.companion: Stop isotretinoin; MRI and MR venography, then LP with opening pressure

items.stem: 15 yo F taking minocycline for acne for 3 months; 3 weeks of daily headache that is worse lying down, brief episodes of graying vision, and horizontal double vision; afebrile and alert; bilateral papilledema, weak abduction of the left eye, full visual fields, otherwise normal neurologic examination
items.key: MRI of the brain with MR venography
items.companion: Excludes mass, hydrocephalus, and venous sinus thrombosis before LP with opening pressure; suspected drug-induced intracranial hypertension
